title: the trust claim does not absorb the callback's own inferred failure channel
notes: poc/src/language/README.md: "SMITHERS1303: an inferred-fallible function crosses a general callback boundary without an explicit Result contract." The callback ownership check never consults the boundary's trust, so it fires identically at a trusted call, an untrusted call, and a local higher-order call. This is one of the three cases that make the acceptance in 09-foreign-calls/a-callback-registered-through-a-trusted-binding-is-accepted narrow: the trust claim covers the call's panic channel and nothing else. The callback's own inferred Result channel, its started async work, and its body's authority are each owned by a rule that never reads the marker.
